Persons to whom warrants of commitment may be addressed and effect of warrants of commitment

[THE STATE PRISONERS ACT, 1850]
[THE STATE PRISONERS ACT, 1850]
ACT No. XXXIV OF 1850
[23rd August, 1850]
(Short
title given by the Short Titles Act, 1897 (14 of 1897).
The Act
has been applied to Baluchistan by the Baluchistan Laws Regu lation, 1913 (2 of
1913), s. 3.
It has
also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas
(,Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G. O. 3 of 1950); and applied in the Federated Areas of
Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 1937, Pt. 1, p. 1499.
This Act has also been extended and shall be deemed to have
been so extended on the 14th day of October, 1955, to the whole of Pakistan,
see the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and
2nd Sch.)
An Act for the better Custody of State Prisoners
(The preamble was omitted by A. O., 1937.)* * * * * *
(Subs. by A.O., 1937, for the original
section.)Persons to whom warrants
of commitment may be addressed and effect of warrants of commitment.[1‑‑‑(1)
The warrant of commitment of any State prisoner, the Bengal State Prisoners
Regulation, 1818, may, if it is issued by virtue of the powers conferred by
that Regulation on the 1818. Central Government, be directed to the commandant
of any fort ress, or the officer in charge of any jail or place, anywhere in (Subs. by
Ordinance 21 of 1960, s. 3 and 2nd Sch., for "any Governor's Province or
Chief Commissioner's Province " (with effect from the 14th Octo ber,
1955).) [Pakistan] and may,
if it is issued by virtue of the powers con ferred by that Regulation on
Provincial Governments, be directed to the commandant of any fortress, or the
officer in charge of any jail or place, anywhere within the Province in
question ; but any such warrant issued under that Regulation, whatever the
powers by virtue of which it is issued, shall be sufficient authority for the
arrest of the State prisoner anywhere in (Subs. by Ordinance 21 of 1960, s. 3 and 2nd Sch., for
"any Governor's Province or Chief Commissioner's Province " (with
effect from the 14th Octo ber, 1955).) [Pakistan] and for his detention until he can be handed over to
the commandant or officer to whom the warrant is directed, or dealt with in
accordance of with sub‑section (1) of section five of the State Prisoners
Act, 1858: Ben Reg. III of 1818, III of 8.
Provided that a State prisoner
shall not be arrested under warrant issued by virtue of the powers conferred by
the said Re gulation on Provincial Governments, except with the consent the
Government of the Province in which he is arrested.
(2) This section applies
throughout (Subs.
ibid., (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and
the Capital of the Federation " which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, Arts.
3(2) and 4, for "British India") [Pakistan] (The words and brackets "(including Berar)" rep. by
the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and II
Sch.)* * *,

Rep. by A. O., 1937
